chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

ʿAlī ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) turned to his children while he was in the state of death, and they were gathered around him. Then he turned to Muhammad ibn ʿAlī and said: “O Muhammad, take this box to your house.”
He said: “Indeed, there was neither any dinar in it nor any dirham, but it was filled with knowledge.”

key_terms.الصُّنْدُوقُ: the box entrusted by the Imam (عليه السلام)
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: the state of dying or the approach of death
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: a silver coin, likewise negated as the box’s contents
key_terms.دِينَارٌ: a gold coin, mentioned here to negate worldly wealth
key_terms.عِلْمًا: knowledge, the true content of the entrusted box
key_terms.وُلْدِهِ: his children or offspring gathered around him

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of the box of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) indicate about the transfer of knowledge to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a moment near the passing of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام), when he entrusted a box to Muhammad ibn ʿAlī. The report clarifies that the box did not contain money, but rather knowledge, indicating the transmission of sacred knowledge and authority within the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام).
